newsitem.title: USA: Projectavision says wins court battle.
newsitem.headline: Projectavision says wins court battle.

text.p: Projectavision Inc said Tuesday that a bid by its founder, Eugene Dolgoff, for a broad receivership has been rejected by the New York Supreme Court.

The company said a court-appointed receiver will have no impact on its ongoing business and day-to-day operations. In particular, its Digital Home Theater televisions are not subject to the receivership, it said.
Dolgoff is no longer with the company.

"This decision vindicates the company, confirming its absolute right to proceed with its business and operations, including sales of the Digital Home Theater, without any interference or impediment from Eugene Dolgoff," President and Chief Executive Martin Holleran said in a statement.

The temporary receiver's authority will be limited to technology on which Dolgoff is listed as an inventor, Projectavision said. The receiver will supervise the patent application process for such technology.
In addition, the receiver will supervise the licensing of such technology, none of which is part of the Digital Home Theater, it said.
